title: How Armstrong got the nickname Satchmo in England
summary: Armstrong explains Satchel Mouth became Satchmo when Percy Brooks greeted him in England; Teagarden's remark follows.

story.theme_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band monikers
story.community_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band names

blocks.x: Satchmo, isn't it? Satchmo, yeah. That's the nickname I picked up in England, you know. In England? Yeah, when I went there in 1932, I met the editor of the Melody Maker, who was Percy Brooks at the time. And at that time, my nickname was Satchel Mouth. See, like the valise, you know what I mean? And now, I don't know, when the train pulled up and Percy Brooks come up, he said, hello, Satchmo, you know. So I said, what'd you say, Daddy? You know, that's what we agreed with. And then I asked my trombone player, who just joined me from Paris, you know. I said, well, why didn't he call me Satchmo? And my name is Satchel Mouth. So the trombone player said, because he thought you had more mouth, you know. Just that easy, I get a nickname. Marsden. Yeah.
Now, I read somewhere, Mr. Armstrong, that Jack Teagarden once described you as just a little guy with a big mouth, but man, can he blow that horn?
